calls.title: BestSeller & GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team is transitioning from Salesforce Commerce Cloud to a new technology stack with Shopify and Sanity to better support smaller brands and improve operational efficiency. The migration includes embedding A/B testing capabilities directly into the CMS, allowing brands to conduct tests independently. The first brand is nearing launch, setting the stage for scaling up to 12-15 storefronts within a year. Data privacy is a concern, with plans for EU-based hosting being addressed by Growth Book’s development of a data center. The team plans to formalize a partnership with Growth Book, focusing on integration and pricing discussions to enhance their testing strategy.
calls.keywords: Bestseller, GrowthBook, Sanity CMS, A/B Testing, Multi-brand Ecommerce, Data Residency

calls.title: Kenneth & James
calls.summary: The team is gearing up to launch the major brand Object, migrating from Contentful to Sanity, which marks a significant move in migrating brands from legacy systems. Kenneth highlighted the ongoing influx of tasks as the team prepares for launch, adopting a pragmatic 'go live and see what happens' approach. The launch schedule is influenced by peak season timing, with brands avoiding go-lives during busy periods. The rollout strategy initially targets about 10 bestseller brands with a dual fee model while allowing for future expansion through renegotiation. They aim to start setup and testing in summer 2023, with close vendor support prioritized in the initial phases. To secure internal buy-in, a strong ROI case is being developed based on analytics to measure performance improvements, with an emphasis on collaboration and in-person meetings to finalize agreements.
calls.keywords: product launch, brand onboarding, commercial structure, testing platform, peak season, partnership negotiation

calls.title: Ryan & James Catch Up (Lego/Bestseller commercials)
calls.summary: The discussion highlighted progress on several key deals, including Skyscanner's confirmed rollout strategy with localized testing, Neco Health's onboarding plans, and the pending contract with Swag Live. The Bestseller deal was emphasized for its complexity involving multiple brands, projected annual experiments, and a tailored pricing strategy. Additionally, the current quarter's revenue forecast was set at approximately $168K with potential upside, supported by backfill deals worth around $130K. Urgent hiring needs were identified to manage increased sales and onboarding demands, particularly for Marcel. Overall, the meeting aimed at aligning efforts to drive successful engagement and revenue growth across multiple accounts.
calls.keywords: experimentation, Bestseller, pricing strategy, onboarding, forecast, contract negotiation

calls.title: GrowthBook & Bestseller Technical/Implementation Demo
calls.summary: The meeting discussed the integration of GrowthBook with Sanity and Shopify, emphasizing that internal teams will manage Snowflake data loading while GrowthBook provides experimentation infrastructure. A central concern was ensuring that all brand users can execute the experimentation workflow within Sanity to minimize tool switching, although some GrowthBook UI/API interaction will still be required for advanced features. The data architecture allows integration with multiple sources, such as BigQuery and Google Analytics. Moreover, a seamless user experience is prioritized, with AI tools introduced for automating experiment management. The meeting concluded with plans for a pilot focused on Sanity integration and feedback-driven refinements to the workflow.
calls.keywords: GrowthBook, Sanity integration, Snowflake analytics, A/B testing, feature flags, experiment workflow

calls.title: James/Kenneth
calls.summary: The meeting focused on establishing a clear and user-friendly workflow for integrating GrowthBook with Sanity, which is essential for brand teams to effectively run tests. Kenneth emphasized understanding how the tool fits into existing operations and proposed alternative workflows. Development plans include a deep-link feature to simplify experiment setup. Both participants discussed aligning testing focus with actual brand needs and leveraging GrowthBook’s UI for results reporting, potentially utilizing AI for summarization. The conversation also touched on the paid proof of concept model, legal alignments, and the crucial need for brand stakeholder engagement to drive adoption and successful rollout, all while acknowledging operational constraints from upcoming vacations.
calls.keywords: GrowthBook, experimentation workflow, PoC, brand adoption, Claude AI, internal alignment
